A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same expert-neuron alignment study, with matching title, authors, and core experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original expert-discovery experiments, MEN alignment correlations, randomized domain comparisons, and analyses across Pythia sizes, training checkpoints, and layers.

after.justification: V2 retains original MEN and Pythia results and adds Semantic Priming Project results, control experiments, and analyses of broader versus narrower concepts.

M1.justification: Both versions use positive and negative sentence sets, per-neuron precision-recall scoring, expertise thresholds, and expert-set overlap. V2's activation notation and temporal max-pooling description expand documentation of the adopted procedure without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds a limited generalization evaluation using 300 Semantic Priming Project pairs spanning unrelated, weakly related, and strongly related concepts (Appendix B). MEN and the ten manually constructed concept domains are retained.

E2.justification: The MEN comparison gains input-embedding-layer representations alongside final-hidden-layer embeddings (Figure 3), and the pilot gains a random-concept-pair comparator (Figure 1). Conversely, the domain analysis removes v1's second baseline, which shuffled broader concepts against intact groups of related concepts. Comparator membership therefore changes across several central analyses.

E3.justification: New designs include the balanced SPP sample of 100 pairs per similarity category at checkpoint 143k and random-weight controls. The reported domain-analysis checkpoints change from 1/512/4k/143k to 1/36k/72k/143k, and within-domain shared-expert percentages are added. The main MEN split, Pythia sizes, and overall checkpoint schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of concept specificity through random-pair overlap, dependence on learning through randomly initialized models, and localization differences between broader and narrower concepts (Appendices I–J). Appendix C additionally reports expert-set sizes across pilot configurations. These substantially expand the supporting analyses beyond v1's existing stability and layer studies.

E5.justification: The SPP analysis introduces mixed-effects regression with sliding-difference coding and concept-specific random intercepts. V2 also adds explicit expert-versus-embedding p-values but removes v1's identification of the domain test as a two-sample permutation test. Eight pilot folds and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals are retained; no increase in repetitions is documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds SPP gradients, input-embedding curves, random-weight and concept-granularity findings, and within-domain overlap results, including 2.24% versus 0.01% random overlap for 12b at 143k. The domain-emergence statement changes from stability around 4k to significance from 36k under revised checkpoint reporting. MEN correlations remain 0.70/0.77/0.79; the reported 58.45% final 12b broader-concept overlap matches the average of v1's per-domain values.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly states the assumption that concept representations align with the canonical basis induced by individual neurons (Section 8), which v1 does not articulate. The added set and activation notation otherwise formalizes the existing procedure; the earlier shared-expert ratio remains described verbally, and no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The claim of human-like hierarchical organization is narrowed to human-interpretable domain organization throughout the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Conversely, the abstract and introduction strengthen close alignment to matching inter-human alignment levels, despite unchanged MEN correlations. These materially revise two central claims.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the taxonomic-containment interpretation with domain clustering and discusses meaningful cross-domain connections. It adds a compression-based explanation of early expert counts, interprets sensitivity to embedding extraction choices, and discusses the absence of broader-versus-narrower localization differences. New limitations address neuron-basis alignment and unresolved causal pathways.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly discloses temporal max pooling of layer outputs before expert scoring. Appendix A corrects the placement of the previously swapped Mistral fact and story examples. Generation prompts, computational-budget information, and licensing disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around traditional word embeddings, mechanistic interpretability, and compression, with corresponding new citations. It distinguishes prior vision findings from the claimed LLM-specific model-size research gap. The earlier discussion separating alignment from task capability, including the Dessì and Sucholutsky–Griffiths references, is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, numbered contributions are introduced, and methods and limitations are expanded. The standalone hierarchy section becomes a domain-organization analysis within the alignment section, while the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains control curves, Figure 3 becomes a two-panel embedding comparison, and domain heatmaps are replaced by network graphs. Numerous per-domain tables become an aggregate table, new SPP and supplementary plots are added, existing layer plots are redrawn, and the benchmark table moves to Appendix G.

improvement.justification: The added embedding comparator, specificity and random-weight controls, and SPP evaluation strengthen empirical support. Clearer implementation details, explicit limitations, and the narrower domain-organization claim also help. These gains support a modest net improvement, tempered by reduced domain-level detail, stronger claims of matching humans without new equivalence evidence, reversed inter/intra-concept descriptions in Figure 1, and Appendix B's ambiguous significance statement using p > 0.0001.
